name: MetroHash
workload: Author's own benchmarks comparing bulk-hashing and small variable-length-key throughput of Metro64/Metro128/Metro128crc against Google's CityHash equivalents.
claimed_speedup: Metro64 ~50% faster than City64 on bulk data, ~15% faster on small keys; Metro128 ~25% faster bulk / ~60% faster small keys vs City128; Metro128crc ~30% faster bulk / ~80% faster small keys vs City128crc
hardware: Haswell-class x86-64 (exact CPU model not stated, only 'Haswell test environment')
tradeoffs: Not designed for adversarial/DoS-resistant hash-table use like SipHash; algorithmically generated rather than hand-designed; C++ classes support both incremental and one-shot hashing; re-licensed Apache-2.0 in 2018 ahead of a v2.0 that never shipped.
caveats: Numbers are relative percentages from the author's own 2015 blog post, not raw throughput figures; exact CPU model, compiler, and flags are not stated, so this falls short of tiers A/B despite being a real, reproducible-in-spirit comparison against CityHash.

name: CLHash
workload: SMHasher bulk-hash speed test, 262144-byte keys, run for many hash functions on the same machine/build in rurban/smhasher.
claimed_speedup: 22932.36 MiB/s (clhash) vs 20853.74 MiB/s (xxh3) in the same SMHasher run, ~10% faster (derived from page data)
compiler_and_flags: CMake Release build, -march=native -std=c++11 per rurban/smhasher CMakeLists.txt; exact GCC/Clang version not stated in the table
hardware: AMD Ryzen 5 3350G 3.6GHz (default smhasher benchmark machine; alternate CPU result tables also published in the same repo)
stars_or_usage: 302 stars; based on Lemire & Kaser, J. Cryptographic Engineering 6(3), 2016
tradeoffs: Requires PCLMULQDQ+SSE4.2 (x64 Haswell or newer) or ARM PMULL crypto extension; fails to build or is slow on unsupported hardware; CLHASH_BITMIX build flag needed to pass SMHasher's avalanche test.
caveats: CLHash's own README only claims '20 to 40x faster than a naive Java-like polynomial hash', not a comparison to xxh3; the xxh3 comparison here is derived from the independent SMHasher shootout table, not from CLHash's own documentation. Repository was transferred from lemire/clhash to the simdhash org.
found_via: GitHub: rurban/smhasher benchmark table (README.md) cross-referenced to simdhash/clhash

name: Meow Hash
workload: SMHasher bulk-hash speed test, 262144-byte keys, x64 AES-NI, run for many hash functions on the same machine/build in rurban/smhasher.
claimed_speedup: MeowHash 29969.81 MiB/s vs xxh3 20853.74 MiB/s (~44% faster), vs wyhash 22640.53 MiB/s (~32% faster), vs City128 14472.20 MiB/s (~107% faster) (derived from page data)
compiler_and_flags: CMake Release build, -march=native -std=c++11 per rurban/smhasher CMakeLists.txt; exact compiler version not stated
hardware: AMD Ryzen 5 3350G 3.6GHz (default table); requires x64 AES-NI
tradeoffs: Hard requirement on x64 AES-NI; after cryptanalysis by Peter Schmidt-Nielsen the project reclassified itself from level-3 to level-1, meaning it is now recommended only for non-adversarial bulk hashing, not for hash tables exposed to attacker-chosen input or for MACs.
caveats: Project's own README makes no quantified vs-baseline claim ('designed to be faster than currently available hashes'); the numeric comparison is derived from the independent SMHasher table, not first-party benchmarks. v0.5/calico was explicitly a 'proposal for the final construction' and appears stalled since 2022 with no v1.0 release.
found_via: GitHub: rurban/smhasher benchmark table (README.md) cross-referenced to cmuratori/meow_hash

name: falkhash
workload: SMHasher bulk-hash speed test, 262144-byte keys, x64 AES-NI (AMD64-targeted design, also runs on Intel), run for many hash functions on the same machine/build in rurban/smhasher.
claimed_speedup: falkhash 52401.48 MiB/s vs xxh3 20853.74 (~2.5x), wyhash 22640.53 (~2.3x), City128 14472.20 (~3.6x) (derived from page data)
compiler_and_flags: CMake Release build, -march=native per rurban/smhasher; author's separate README reports 0.074-0.25 cycles/byte across GCC 4.9.2 / clang 3.5.0 / MSVC 19 on several older CPUs, but without any baseline comparison
hardware: AMD Ryzen 5 3350G 3.6GHz (smhasher table); author's own tests used AMD Opteron 6376, Intel Xeon E5645, Core i7 970 and Core i7 4712HQ
tradeoffs: Author explicitly labels it 'Exotic Probably Shitty Hash', not intended as a rigorously designed general-purpose hash; heavily reliant on aesenc so unportable and slow without AES-NI; author states it was found by 'randomly testing things until it passed smhasher'.
caveats: Author's own README gives no direct vs-xxHash/wyhash/CityHash numbers, only raw cycles/byte figures on decade-old hardware. The competitive comparison is derived entirely from the independent SMHasher shootout table. Low notability (48 stars) and unmaintained since 2015, included per DO-NOT-EXCLUDE rules since abandonment/low stars are not grounds to skip a non-D-tier entry.
found_via: GitHub: rurban/smhasher benchmark table (README.md) cross-referenced to gamozolabs/falkhash

name: UMASH
workload: SMHasher bulk-hash speed test, 262144-byte keys, run for many hash functions on the same machine/build in rurban/smhasher.
claimed_speedup: umash64 26628.37 MiB/s and umash32_hi 26601.23 MiB/s vs xxh3 20853.74 MiB/s, ~28% faster (derived from page data)
compiler_and_flags: CMake Release build, -march=native per rurban/smhasher; UMASH's own README separately reports 10.9 byte/cycle (39.5 GiB/s) on an AMD EPYC 7713 with a gcc-compatible compiler and CLMUL
hardware: AMD Ryzen 5 3350G 3.6GHz (smhasher table); AMD EPYC 7713 and Apple M1 performance cores (author's own numbers)
tradeoffs: Requires x86-64 CLMUL or aarch64 PMULL crypto extension; provides a proven almost-universal collision bound unlike most fast non-crypto hashes, but the ABI around umash_params_prepare is explicitly not yet finalized.
caveats: UMASH's own README frames its throughput as merely 'comparable to' XXH3/MeowHash/HalftimeHash, not faster; the beat-xxh3 claim here is derived from the independent SMHasher shootout table, where it edges out xxh3 by ~28% on that specific hardware/build.

name: lanehash
workload: Own benchmark harness on AMD Ryzen 5 7600 (Zen 4): 4B-64KiB inputs, cycles/hash and bytes/cycle, same binary/buffers for lanehash, xxh3 (AVX-512), and rapidhash v3; the AES variant (lanehash64/lanehash128 in SMHasher naming) is separately timed on different hardware inside rurban/smhasher.
claimed_speedup: 64KiB bulk: 27.0 B/cycle (lanehash) vs 18.5 (xxh3 AVX-512) vs 8.8 (rapidhash v3), ~46% faster than xxh3; 4KiB: 21.8 vs 12.8 vs 8.1 B/cycle. Short 4-16B keys are actually slower than xxh3 (11.4-12.0 vs 9.5-10.1 cycles/hash). Independently, the SMHasher table shows the AES variant (lanehash64/128) at ~43.8-44.3 GB/s bulk on an older Ryzen 5 3350G, above that table's xxh3 (20.9 GB/s) and wyhash (22.6 GB/s) figures.
compiler_and_flags: cargo build --release (default profile), runtime dispatch selecting AVX-512; exact rustc version not stated
tradeoffs: By the author's own admission, dependent-chain latency is worse than rapidhash for 4-16B and ~128B inputs; scalar fallback is much slower than the SIMD backends; core implementation is Rust, with a separate lanehash-c crate/build for C/C++ consumption.
caveats: Extremely new and unreviewed (about a week old at time of search, 1 star, size 1246 mostly Rust); numbers are first-party with partial methodology (CPU model given, exact compiler version not). The independent SMHasher table corroborates a large win for the AES variant on different, older hardware, which raises confidence somewhat but doesn't move the tier past C per the partial-methodology rule.
found_via: GitHub: rurban/smhasher benchmark table (lanehash64/lanehash128 rows, tagged AES only) traced to ccipherx/lanehash

name: FarmHash
workload: SMHasher bulk-hash speed test, 262144-byte keys; FarmHash32 uses the SSE4.1/AVX code path, run alongside CityHash and xxh3 on the same machine/build in rurban/smhasher.
claimed_speedup: FarmHash32 22136.14 MiB/s vs xxh3 20853.74 MiB/s (~6% faster) and vs its own predecessor CityHash (City32 5745.83 MiB/s, ~285% faster) (derived from page data)
compiler_and_flags: CMake Release build, -march=native per rurban/smhasher; FarmHash's own build docs separately recommend -mavx -maes -O3
hardware: AMD Ryzen 5 3350G 3.6GHz; requires x64 SSE4.1/AVX for the fast FarmHash32 path
stars_or_usage: 659 stars; historically Google's successor to CityHash, widely vendored (e.g. in Abseil-adjacent and RocksDB-era codebases)
tradeoffs: Selects among many internal hash variants via conditional compilation/GCC multiversioning depending on target CPU features and endianness; implementation is described by its own README as 'fairly complex'; in this table only the 32-bit variant clears xxh3, and by a modest ~6% margin — FarmHash64/FarmHash128 are both slower than xxh3 on the same run.
caveats: FarmHash's own README/NEWS make no explicit quantified speed claim vs xxHash or CityHash (only general SMHasher quality-testing notes); the win here is derived from the independent SMHasher table and is a narrow margin for FarmHash32 specifically.
found_via: GitHub: gh search repos "farmhash" --sort stars, cross-referenced to rurban/smhasher benchmark table
